correctness.rationale: For each fixed finite horizon the actual mean rates define a constant, interior equilibrium. The weighted Jacobian-flux telescope gives an exact derivative of quadratic energy, and cumulative edge inventory adds an exact derivative converting the weighted instantaneous flux into terminal throughput. Algebra yields identity (1) without any periodicity or averaging hypotheses. Strict curvature of \(W(y)=(1-y^2)^{-1/2}\), separate treatment of the branch \(s\leq -2\), and an explicitly positive quadratic expansion at \(y=b\) force a uniform dissipation lower bound on the entire compact rate box. The bounded storage term proves the \(O(T^{-1})\) inequality for every measurable rate control, all initial states, all horizons. A one-site constant-rate orbit proves the transient-order sharpness. The package verifier passed 3170 exact-rational checks for dimensions 1–3; finite checks are supplementary, not proofs.

originality.rationale: The exact weighted edge-dissipation ingredients, curvature no-gain mechanism, and periodic equality rigidity are prior work of Zhou (arXiv:2610.10602v1). Zhou §7 expressly poses extension beyond common periodic forcing as future work. The assessed contribution is the unaveraged terminal-flux/inventory storage identity, coercive quadratic penalty uniform in arbitrary horizon means, arbitrary measurable controls and initial states, and sharp transient order. It is not a claim to originate energy-storage or dissipativity methods. The nearest classical RFM proof (arXiv:2607.25435v1) is for linear vacancy and periodic orbits. The 2021 periodic-optimization article and the 2026 nonlinear cascade abstract do not provide a published statement dominating all new quantifiers. A prior equivalent nonperiodic dissipativity reformulation remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The motivating article §7 identifies non-common periodicity and general recurrence as a concrete mathematical gap. The result extends that question to arbitrary measurable bounded controls, provides a finite-time bound valid without attraction, adds a nontrivial uniform L² turnpike deficit that yields near-optimal-state rigidity, and proves by an exact scalar orbit that \(O(T^{-1})\) is the best possible initial-transient order. This is a natural transport/throughput invariant with a rigorous operational interpretation, not a routine normalization test or unmotivated finite slice. The fixed quadratic class, though specialized, is an explicitly central natural model in the motivating article.
